                    ### Question
                    A 27-year-old man is running on the treadmill at his gym. His blood pressure prior to beginning his workout was 110/72. Which of the following changes in his cardiovascular system may be seen in this man now that he is exercising?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Increased systemic vascular resistance
opb. Decreased heart rate
opc. Decreased stroke volume
opd. Decreased systemic vascular resistance
ope. Decreased blood pressure

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
During exercise, the cardiovascular system undergoes several changes to meet the increased demand for oxygen and nutrients by the muscles. Key consensus points include: 1) Increased heart rate and cardiac output to enhance blood flow; 2) Decreased systemic vascular resistance due to vasodilation in active muscles, which allows for greater blood flow without a significant increase in blood pressure; 3) Stroke volume may initially increase due to enhanced venous return and contractility, rather than decrease. Therefore, the most accurate changes observed in this 27-year-old man exercising on the treadmill would be a decreased systemic vascular resistance and an increased heart rate, leading to increased cardiac output. The options of increased systemic vascular resistance, decreased heart rate, decreased stroke volume, and decreased blood pressure are inconsistent with these physiological responses during exercise.
